generalizedRange: Red River basin of northern Viet Nam and Yunnan, and the lower Yangtze floodplain of eastern China — today a few lakes west of Hanoi and one zoo in Suzhou
hook: Two known alive. One is over 100 years old. The other’s sex is unknown.

story.text: The largest freshwater turtle on earth is a softshell: a bony plate ringed with cartilage under leathery skin, olive with yellow spots.
It is secretive, surfacing and basking rarely, keeping to the depths of large turbid lakes.
In Hanoi it is the Hoan Kiem turtle, from a fifteenth-century legend of a turtle rising to reclaim King Le Loi’s sword.
In the 1970s to 1990s it was hunted for food while its wetlands were dammed or turned to rice fields.
On 19 January 2016 Cu Rua, Great Grandfather Turtle, some 170 kilograms, was found floating in Hoan Kiem Lake, one of four known alive.
At Suzhou Zoo a pair together since 2008 nested, every egg infertile; the female died 13 April 2019 after a fifth artificial insemination.
A turtle netted in Dong Mo Lake on 22 October 2020 proved female: a male and a female were known again.
On 23 April 2023 keepers found a Dong Mo turtle dead — 93 kilograms, nearly 156 centimetres — likely the 2020 female.
As of 2024 two are known: the Suzhou male, over 100, and one of unknown sex in Xuan Khanh Lake, found by DNA in lake water.
To witness the Yangtze giant softshell turtle is to watch a still lake for a head that may never rise, hoping the water holds more.

reproduction.text: A female can lay more than 50 eggs a clutch, three or four clutches a year, and stay fertile past 90 — yet the Suzhou pair, together since 2008, never produced a fertile egg.

insight.text: As of 2024 the Xuan Khanh turtle has never been caught: its existence rests on one unclear photograph from 2017 and traces of its DNA sieved from the lake water.

programs.title: Rafetus swinhoei Project, Viet Nam
programs.summary: Keeps full-time local watchers on Dong Mo and Xuan Khanh lakes, runs interview surveys and eDNA sampling across northern Viet Nam’s rivers and lakes for undiscovered animals, and works with Hanoi’s fisheries and forest-protection agencies on capture, sexing, and a breeding plan.

programs.title: Swinhoe’s Giant Softshell Turtle, Vietnam program
programs.summary: With ATP, WCS, and the Government of Vietnam, uses visual surveys, drone and camera-trap searches, eDNA analysis, and capture-and-release to find and confirm individuals in Dong Mo and Xuan Khanh lakes.
